children: The $115 bln oil major picked Ian Tyler after Albert Manifold’s rocky exit. His BAE Systems pedigree may ease governance jitters. But weak returns during his time as CEO of building firm Balfour Beatty suggests Meg O’Neill may have to drive cost cuts and disposals on her own.
Full view will be published shortly.

BP on September 2 appointed Ian Tyler, former CEO of UK building group ‌Balfour Beatty, as its permanent chair after it fired Albert Manifold in May, citing governance and conduct concerns.

Amanda Blanc, BP's senior independent director, who oversaw Manifold and Tyler's appointments, will not seek re-election at BP's 2027 annual general meeting and will step down once her successor has been found, BP said.

Tyler, who also chairs building materials firm Grafton Group and is a senior independent director at mining company Anglo American, joined BP's board in April 2025 and replaced Manifold on an interim basis in May 2026.
BP’s share price rose by 0.2% at 0720 GMT on September 2.
